standard_prerequisites.name: Weakly associated primes under a flat pullback
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, label divisors-lemma-weakly-ass-pullback, invoked at proof line 325
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the easy implication: a weakly associated prime downstairs pulls back to one upstairs because the morphism is flat.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite flat algebra over a local ring is free, and weakly associated points under a finite morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-finite-flat-local (proof line 336); Divisors, label divisors-lemma-weakly-associated-finite (proof line 348)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives that the localised algebra is a free module of some rank n at least one, so that the pushforward of the pulled back module has the same weakly associated primes as the original downstairs, and the second pushes a weakly associated point through the finite morphism.

core_obligations: Get the easy implication: flatness of the morphism makes a weakly associated prime downstairs a weakly associated prime of the pullback, which is the pullback statement for flat morphisms (proof lines 324-325).

Reduce to an affine local computation: assume a point t of the pullback module is weakly associated, take an affine open neighbourhood of its image and write the situation as a finite flat algebra B over A with the module M tensored with B; because B is finite flat over the local ring, its localisation at the prime is free of rank n at least one (there is a point lying over the image), so by looking at stalks the image point is weakly associated for the module if and only if it is weakly associated for the pushforward of the pullback (proof lines 326-345).

Conclude: since t is weakly associated for the pullback, its image is weakly associated for the pushforward of the pullback by the statement for finite morphisms, and hence weakly associated for the original module (proof lines 346-349).
proof_roadmap: Flat pullback gives one implication (proof lines 324-325).
Finite flatness reduces the other implication to a free local algebra and a stalk computation (proof lines 326-345).
Push the weakly associated point through the finite morphism (proof lines 346-349).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a finite flat morphism the weakly associated points of a pullback are exactly the points lying over weakly associated points of the original module (statement lines 311-321, tag 05FN). One implication is the flat pullback statement, but the converse needs a genuine local computation: one passes to an affine neighbourhood, uses that a finite flat algebra over a local ring is free of a rank which is at least one because a point lies over the image, concludes by looking at stalks that the image point is weakly associated for the pushforward of the pullback, and then applies the statement on weakly associated points under a finite morphism. The local computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
